why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repo. Every command needs only files that exist (bin/csv2json.js, test/*.js, README.md) and the `test` script in package.json, so `npm test` runs. The printf pipelines, `; echo "exit=$?"`, `| od -c` and `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` all have valid shell syntax and the right arguments. The JS strings in the builder's test cases are escaped correctly: `'[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n'` is the JSON tab escape. The verifier does not tell anyone to run the missing `npm run test:cli`; it only says the verifier may run it if the head adds that script. `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv` is example text for the README, not a step to run. `node bin/csv2json.js foo --tsv` is an advisory illustration ("e.g."), and the CLI ignores extra arguments anyway. No command breaks the criterion.
